text:
Connor Dewar hasn't recorded a point in ten straight games, and the chances have thinned out too: 3.2 expected points over the run. He's playing 13 and a half minutes a night as a checking center for a Penguins team that has won two of his last ten.

The contrast with last season is sharp. Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among 401 forwards in wins above replacement in 2025-26, a big number for a depth player, though it ran ahead of his chances. That kind of season usually comes back down, and this one has.

The on-ice numbers are better than the points. Pittsburgh gets 56% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about four and a half points better than without him. DK Pittsburgh Sports argued last week that his line with Filip Hallander and Elmer Soderblom deserved to stay together.

He's a penalty killer and a forechecker (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him dumping the puck in on most entries). What to watch: a goal to snap the drought. The process says he's due something, if not much.
